title: Tree-size representation of a padded language
statement: Let $\ell,T':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $\ell(n)\le n$ for every $n$, and let $F_n$ be a Boolean function on assignments to $\ell(n)$ inputs. Suppose that for every $n$, $2^{\ell(n)}(\ell(n)+1)+1\le T'(n)$. Then the language of Boolean lists accepted by the padded circuits has a family of tree circuits, one on each input length, whose size at length $n$ is at most $T'(n)$ and which accepts exactly the lists in that language.
hypotheses_covered: $\ell$ and $T'$ map natural numbers to natural numbers
For every $n$, $F_n$ is a Boolean function on assignments to $\ell(n)$ inputs
